R.thresholds: R2 requires >=100k distinct grade-appropriate learners with usable local-language/entry support and a residual gap. R3 requires >=1M such learners. Existing textbooks must be excluded only where they already supply the proposed usable package, not just because a catalog entry exists.

scenarios.cautious: RU if the exact local varieties and grade population remain unresolved; unknown is not zero.
scenarios.baseline: R2 for the DRC/Uganda bounded country package.
scenarios.favorable: R3 when completed locality-specific outputs cover a million-scale residual; no R4 inherited from Tanzania.

R.base_basis: The current package targets only two grade/country routes, so whole-family 200M speech estimates and legacy Tanzanian R4 are irrelevant to its first-output audience. A hundred-thousand-to-million-scale opportunity is plausible across these large systems but an exact language-by-grade-by-supply joint denominator is absent.
R.endpoint_semantics: Conditional qualitative judgment endpoints; not observed-benefit bounds or confidence limits.

S.calibration_type: source-informed provisional planning judgment, not a confidence interval or observed effect
S.basis: New DRC ministry inventory evidences early-grade Kiswahili books and literacy packages. Scarcity now concerns verified missing components, independent worked feedback, accessible/offline reuse and regional fit; Uganda L2 supply is a separate problem.
